Subject: Where do Redwood requests get processed? quick QnA

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at NovaBlue is excited about the latency improvements. Security has one follow-up we need answered before moving the procurement request forward: for requests that hit Redwood's hosted API, can you give a concise breakdown of where the data is processed (region by region), what subprocessors may touch tokens or logs, and how cross-border hops are handled? We also need a short note on deletion responsibilities and how long cached/stored artefacts (e.g., KV cache, logs, embeddings) persist.

We'd appreciate a short written Q&A and any diagrams you can share. If you prefer, scheduling a 30-minute architecture call with Priya and your compliance lead works.

Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear ask and great meeting yesterday.

High-level answer (summary):
- Hosted API: default execution occurs in the region selected by the customer at request time or by the org's region preference (we expose a region parameter and per-account default).
- Processing regions we operate (hosted): US (us-central-1, us-east-1), EU (eu-west-1), APAC (ap-southeast-1). Specific availability depends on the model and instance pool at the time of request.
- Subprocessors: our runtime may interact with (a) cloud infra providers that host compute (e.g., AWS/GCP/Azure regional pools), (b) logging/metrics vendors for operational traces, and (c) optional third-party vector stores when customers enable managed embeddings.
- Cross-border hops: requests are routed to a regional pool; we attempt region affinity by policy. If regional capacity is insufficient, requests can be routed to a compatible pool in another region per routing policy; we document failover paths and can provide an explicit list for your account.
- Deletion responsibilities: Redwood deletes customer-managed data on request per the agreed retention policy and can automate deletion on account termination. Cached KV/embeddings have configurable TTLs; default retention for transient caches is 24 hours, logs are retained 30 days by default (configurable), and embeddings stored in managed services are retained until explicitly deleted.

I've attached a short processing map and a CSV inventory of common subprocessors. Priya (copied) is our solutions engineer and can walk through a model-by-model execution map if you'd like. Ben handles SOC evidence if you need root-cause logs or audit exports.

Proposed next steps: 1) I can send a one-page evidence pack for EU-only routing for your legal review; 2) Priya or I can run a short walkthrough with your security team this week. Which do you prefer?

Thanks,

Thanks Soojin — that summary helps. A couple of clarifying questions from security/legal:
1) When requests are routed due to capacity limits, do any request payloads or intermediate artifacts leave the original geographic region before execution? We need to know if PII could transit outside our specified geography even transiently.
2) For managed embeddings, which third-party vector stores are used by default and where are those stores located? If a customer wants to ensure embeddings never leave EU, can Redwood lock embeddings to an EU-only store?
3) For deletion: please confirm the SLA for deletion requests (e.g., within X hours/days), and whether deletion from cloud infra/backups is guaranteed within the same SLA or handled on a best-effort basis.

If you can provide short plain-language answers and mark anything that would require an enterprise contract amendment, that would be ideal. We can take the evidence pack after that.

Appreciate it,
Ethan

Subject: Re: Where do Redwood requests get processed? quick QnA

Hi Ethan — Hannah from Redwood Compliance here. I pulled answers together below; I kept them short and noted where a contractual amendment is typically required.

1) Transient cross-border transit: 
- By default, requests are routed to a regional execution pool; payloads are only routed outside the designated region when a routing policy triggers (capacity, maintenance, or customer-configured fallback). During such failovers, request payloads may be encrypted in transit and processed in the alternate region; we can configure strict routing to prevent cross-border routing for regulated customers (this is an enterprise control and requires a Dedicated or Private deployment addendum).

2) Managed embeddings and vector stores:
- Default managed embeddings are stored in Redwood-managed vector stores hosted in the same region as execution when the customer enables "regional embeddings". If a customer uses our managed embeddings without regional locking, the service may place indexes in replicated regional stores for availability. Third-party vector stores we integrate with by request include Pinecone and Milvus (customers may bring their own).
- EU-only guarantee: We offer an EU-only embedding option for Hosted customers as a contractual commitment (requires configuration and a small premium). For full guarantee across backups and failover, we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or a Dedicated contract.

3) Deletion SLA and backups:
- Deletion SLA: standard hosted customers: we acknowledge deletion requests within 24 hours and complete primary-store deletion within 72 hours. Log and backup purges follow retention schedules and are typically best-effort for removal from cloud provider-managed snapshots; for enterprise customers we include a clearance SLA in the contract (e.g., 30-day backup purge commitment) and provide audit evidence.

4) Evidence and artifacts we can provide now:
- Processing map (attached) showing hop paths and failover rules.
- Subprocessor inventory with region annotations (attached CSV).
- SOC2 scope and sample audit export (available on request).

Contract notes: any hard restriction preventing transient cross-border hops or a legally-binding EU-only residency guarantee for all artifacts (including backups, caches, and third-party indices) is treated as an enterprise feature and will be reflected in the Dedicated/Private addendum.

Next steps: If you confirm you'd like the EU-only embedding commitment and explicit failover exclusions, Soojin and Priya can put together a short amendment and pricing estimate; we can also schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team this week.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
